thread:
amy_cs: heads-up — customer 'OrbitHealth' reporting p99 jump on /v1/embeddings to ~4s starting ~09:11 UTC. Ticket #CH-1129.
sam: thanks. any repro payloads or curl examples from support?
amy_cs: yes, attached snippet they used: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"input": "...long docs..."}'` they said spikes coincide with large batch requests and lots of short session ids in headers.
maria: looking at metrics now. I see a sharp rise in prefix cache miss rate at 09:10:58 — miss rate jumped from 12% -> 78% for embedding-serving nodes in us-west-2. KV eviction rate also spiked.
jordan: can you paste the p95/p99 numbers around that window?
maria: p95 went from 220ms -> 1.2s, p99 -> 3.9s. CPU/GPU usage unchanged. Disk i/o fine.
sam: sounds like cache warmup / key cardinality issue rather than backend saturation. any header patterns?
amy_cs: customer noted they inject X-Client-Session header with per-request GUIDs for tracing.
kai: that screams cache key entropy. if prefix cache includes request headers in key, we might be generating unique prefix keys per session.
maria: confirmed — prefix key uses `customer_id + route + normalized_headers` but normalization excludes X-Client-Session; header whitelist logic only applied in a few routes. looks like a recent change in header canonicalization (PR #3792) loosened header filtering.
jordan: ok repro steps: 1) send burst of 200 requests with unique X-Client-Session 2) observe prefix miss rate and KV evictions 3) p99 spikes on subsequent requests. I have a tiny repro script, dropping in #dev-tools.
sam: immediate mitigation options?
maria: can roll back PR quickly but I prefer feature-flag short-term: `prefix_canonicalize_headers=true` -> forces canonicalization and strips non-whitelisted headers for cache key. I can flip it on the canary pool in 30s.
kai: also recommend enabling `warmup-drip=true` to stagger KV prefetches and lower eviction churn. set drip_rate to 50 keys/sec per shard.
sam: do it — flip the flag on canary first. keep me posted with p95.
maria: flipping on canary now...
ops-bot: deploy triggered: feature-flag prefix_canonicalize_headers=true on canary pool (deployed by maria).
maria: canary metrics: p99 down to 1.0s, p95 down to 450ms within 120s. miss rate dropped to 18%.
jordan: good sign. can we scope to prod rollout? recommend 10% -> 50% over 15m if no regressions.
kai: while rollout is ongoing, create a temporary routing rule to send high-cardinality customers to a dedicated isolate pool to protect others. also add a short term ttl bump for prefetched items (ttl + 30s) to reduce rewarm churn.
sam: agreed. maria, start the gradual rollout. jordan, open an action item for a postmortem and long term fix. amy_cs, communicate to customer that we're rolling mitigations and ask for their header usage details so we can offer guidance.
amy_cs: pinged customer with update + asked for sample headers. they're appreciative. :thumbsup:
maria: rolling to 10% -> 50% now. monitoring.
ops-bot: rollout progress: 10% -> 50% (elapsed 12m). no alerts.
maria: 50% -> 100% complete. p95 stabilized at ~300ms, p99 ~600ms across the fleet. miss rate baseline ~14%.
sam: nice. long-term fixes: 1) enforce header whitelist at ingress (reject or strip high-cardinality headers by default) 2) add prefix key hashing normalization with truncation to limit cardinality 3) implement LFU-ish eviction for prefix cache to favor hot prefixes 4) add dashboard alert for sudden miss-rate deltas.
jordan: I'll own the postmortem doc (PMM-CH-1129) and include repro, timeline, root cause (header-whitelist regression + cache warmup drip insufficient), mitigations, and follow-ups.
kai: I'll file infra ticket to prototype LFU cache and splay warmup.
amy_cs: customer closed the urgent ticket, will keep it open till tomorrow for verification. thanks everyone. :heart:
sam: great response. please add any artifacts (graphs, trace ids, the tiny repro script) to the ticket. closing this thread once postmortem is up.
maria: uploaded graphs and a short changelog to CH-1129.
jordan: postmortem draft shared. tagging eng-runtime leadership for visibility.
